thread:
kevin_support: FYI customer reported bursts of 429s this morning after a traffic spike, asks for repro steps and headers. attaching initial details below.

emma_cs: Copied. Customer says errors started at ~2026-03-16T09:12:30Z and saw ~120 429s in 3m.

kevin_support: Example curl they ran (sanitized API key):

kevin_support: ```
curl -i -X POST 
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hello"}'
```

kevin_support: Response snippet they pasted: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d4e
X-Rate-Limit-Limit: 60
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0
X-Rate-Limit-Reset: 1679033599

matt_eng: That X-Request-ID looks like one from our edge. Can you ask for 3 full request IDs spaced across the spike and a HAR? We need timestamps and response headers.

kevin_support: Requested three request IDs + full HAR + approximate client concurrency and client region. Asking customer to run curl with --trace-ascii.

emma_cs: Customer sent one more request id: req_9f8e7d6c5b, and a short log showing repeated 429s with Retry-After 2 or 3. They also said this app opens 10 concurrent connections per instance and had a deploy earlier at 08:50Z.

riley_sre: Quick checks: 1) Is this a per-key quota or org-level reserved capacity? 2) Any Dedicated pool failover at that time? I'll check routing logs.

matt_eng: We saw a brief spike in token throughput in region eu-west-1 at 09:12Z with many short sessions. Autoscaler didn't add nodes quickly because short-lived bursts. Likely client-side concurrency caused per-key limit.

kevin_support: Customer also pasted a billing/quota panel screenshot showing daily token cap at 100k and usage at 98.7k at 09:10Z.

riley_sre: Ok that supports quota exhaustion. Still want full HAR and server-side trace. Ask them to run our debug-bundle script to collect traces and signed logs (one-liner below).

riley_sre: ```
# ask customer to run from a workstation that hits the API
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{url_effective} %{time_total}\n' -D headers.txt -X POST \ 
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"probe"}'
# attach headers.txt and client-side HAR from browser or CLI trace
```

kevin_support: Sent that to customer and asked for timestamps for each failing request. Also requested server X-Request-ID for each.

emma_cs: Customer replied with 3 more request ids: req_a111, req_b222, req_c333 and attached headers.txt for one failing request: shows Retry-After: 2, X-Request-ID: req_b222.

matt_eng: I'm pulling logs for those IDs. Also check quota window: X-Rate-Limit-Reset in their snippet mapped to 09:15Z UTC. That explains short Retry-After values.

riley_sre: If they hit per-minute quota then bursts will return 429 until reset. Suggest we advise exponential backoff with jitter, and optionally request a quota bump for this customer if traffic pattern is legitimate.

kevin_support: Customer asks if we can reproduce internally. Can we create a curl loop to mimic 10 connections * 5 instances for 3 minutes?

matt_eng: Yes, we can run a repro from our infra-test runner. I'll coordinate a load job and attach our HAR + server logs. Expect to see 'X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0' and 429s.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline:infra-test-runner triggered load job id load_20260316_001 by matt_eng.

matt_eng: Load job finished. Repro notes: we hit per-key per-minute limit after ~55s with similar Retry-After 3 headers. Collected server logs for req_b222 pattern. Attaching summarized evidence in ticket.

kevin_support: Shared repro logs and recommended short-term mitigation: reduce concurrent connections to 3 per instance, add exponential backoff + 429-aware retry, consider rate-limit increase ticket.

emma_cs: Customer accepted mitigation, will throttle client. They requested we keep ticket open to confirm no more 429s after tomorrow's morning traffic.

riley_sre: Closing loop: recommend docs link on client-side knobs + sample backoff code. Also flag for product to evaluate smoother autoscaling for short bursts.

kevin_support: Thanks team :thumbsup: closing for now but will re-open if customer sees more 429s after changes."
